hi marc,

i was just talking to colleagues about this and realize that I have not explained what I want to do very well so I'll start from the beginning.

We want to compare two assemblages using the moetdo from Giacomini and Galetti's paper called "An index for defaunation". The index is essentially a bray-curtis dissimilarity index. 

So what we want to do is use unmarked to estimate the occupancy probability of 10 species in two sites and then compare these. But we also want to give confidence intervals so have to incorproate the uncertainty associated with the occupancy estimates. To do this the authors suggest to use a monte carlo method to take samples from the probability distribution. So I would use this to generate random samples of occupancy probability and then calculate the defaunation index 10000 times and then use this to generate the 95% CIs. So what i think i need is somethign like a posterior distribution of occupancy probability. Or do you have any other suggestions?

Thanks for your help
- Jesse

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] probability distribution
parts:
Dear Jesse,

I don't know the method you're mentioning, but here are some comments about occupancy and comparing stuff:

- If you have two sites, and only two sites, you can't really estimate an occupancy probability. You need spatial reps for that. If you mean you have two sites and then within each of them multiple reps (e.g., point counts), then it's OK.
- if you do have reps and can therefore estimate occupancy, the best to compare occupancy between the two "sites" = regions would be to fit a model with species random effects and a fixed region effect. If this turns out to be "important" (used to say "significant"), then there's your answer.
- I just realize that this really belongs into the realm of multi-species occupancy models and hence a full, integrated analysis cannot be done in unmarked. Although: you could use the trick used in the MacKenzie et al. 2006/2017 occupancy book  of using species as sites to make inferences about a community. But better would be to fit the community model in the Bayesian mode of inference.
- If you just want to have 20 estimates of occupancy, along with  a 95% CI, as an input for some other analysis, then you can easily get that in unmarked and there is no need to do any bootstrapping for the CIs. Just see the documentation.

Best regards  --- Marc
